questions.stem: A 24-year-old man has a closed fracture of the right tibial shaft after a motorcycle crash. The leg is placed in a long splint. Eight hours later, he has severe, burning pain in the front of the leg that is not relieved by intravenous opioids. His vital signs are: temperature 37.4°C, pulse 108/min, blood pressure 134/82 mm Hg. Laboratory studies: creatine kinase 5,600 U/L, potassium 4.9 mEq/L, creatinine 1.0 mg/dL. The skin over the leg is tense. Passive flexion of the toes toward the sole causes intense pain in the front of the leg. Sensation is reduced only over the skin between the first and second toes. The dorsalis pedis pulse is palpable. Which compartment of the leg is most likely affected?
questions.explanation: The **anterior compartment** holds the toe and ankle extensors and the **deep fibular nerve**, which supplies the skin of the **first web space** of the foot. Rising pressure causes pain out of proportion and pain when the trapped muscles are **passively stretched** (toe flexion stretches the extensors); a palpable pulse does not rule it out. The **lateral compartment** holds the superficial fibular nerve, so it would cause numbness over most of the dorsum of the foot and pain on passive inversion.
questions.explanation_pt: O **compartimento anterior** contém os extensores dos dedos e do tornozelo e o **nervo fibular profundo**, que inerva a pele do **primeiro espaço interdigital** do pé. A pressão crescente causa dor desproporcional e dor ao **estiramento passivo** dos músculos presos (a flexão dos dedos estira os extensores); um pulso palpável não exclui o diagnóstico. O **compartimento lateral** contém o nervo fibular superficial, então causaria dormência na maior parte do dorso do pé e dor à inversão passiva.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old professional volleyball player has had a dull ache at the back of his right shoulder for several months. Exam shows wasting of the muscle below the spine of the right scapula. External rotation of the right arm with the elbow at his side is weak. The first part of arm abduction is strong, and the deltoid looks normal. Sensation over the shoulder is normal. MRI shows a small cyst next to the posterior glenoid labrum, and the supraspinatus muscle looks normal. At which site is a nerve most likely compressed?
questions.explanation: The **suprascapular nerve** supplies the supraspinatus first and then passes around the **spinoglenoid notch** to reach the **infraspinatus**. A lesion at that notch (for example a cyst from the labrum, or repeated overhead stretch in volleyball) weakens only the infraspinatus, so external rotation is weak and abduction is spared. Compression at the **suprascapular notch** happens before the supraspinatus branch leaves, so the supraspinatus would also waste and the start of abduction would be weak.
questions.explanation_pt: O **nervo supraescapular** inerva primeiro o supraespinal e depois contorna a **incisura espinoglenoidal** para chegar ao **infraespinal**. Uma lesão nessa incisura (por exemplo, um cisto originado do lábio glenoidal, ou estiramento repetido do nervo nos movimentos acima da cabeça, como no vôlei) enfraquece só o infraespinal, então a rotação externa fica fraca e a abdução é poupada. A compressão na **incisura supraescapular** (incisura da escápula) ocorre antes da saída do ramo do supraespinal, então o supraespinal também atrofiaria e o início da abdução estaria fraco.

questions.stem: A 76-year-old woman trips at home and falls onto her left side. She cannot stand, and the left leg is shortened and turned outward. Her vital signs are: pulse 94/min, blood pressure 150/88 mm Hg, respirations 16/min. Hemoglobin is 12.6 g/dL. X-rays show a displaced fracture of the left femoral neck just below the head, inside the joint capsule. The surgeon explains that if the fragments were fixed with screws, the femoral head might later die, so a hip replacement is planned. Tearing of the branches of which artery is mainly responsible for this risk?
choices: Artery of the ligament of the head of the femur
questions.explanation: In adults the femoral head gets most of its blood from **retinacular branches of the medial circumflex femoral artery**, which run up the back of the neck under the capsule. A displaced **intracapsular** neck fracture tears them, so the head is at high risk of **avascular necrosis**. The **artery of the ligament of the head** (from the obturator artery) enters the head directly, which makes it tempting, but in adults it supplies only a small area near the fovea and cannot keep the head alive.
questions.explanation_pt: No adulto, a cabeça do fêmur recebe a maior parte do sangue dos **ramos retinaculares da artéria circunflexa femoral medial**, que sobem pela face posterior do colo, sob a cápsula. Uma fratura **intracapsular** desviada do colo os rompe, então a cabeça tem alto risco de **necrose avascular**. A **artéria do ligamento da cabeça do fêmur** (ramo da artéria obturatória) entra direto na cabeça, o que a torna tentadora, mas no adulto irriga só uma pequena área perto da fóvea e não consegue manter a cabeça viva.

questions.stem: In an experiment, researchers remove the somites next to the developing wing bud of an early chick embryo. The wing grows to a normal length. Its cartilage and bones have a normal shape and number, and its tendons and connective tissue are present, but it contains no skeletal muscle. The bones and cartilage of the wing most likely came from which embryonic tissue?
choices: Somatic (parietal) layer of the lateral plate mesoderm
Splanchnic (visceral) layer of the lateral plate mesoderm
questions.explanation: Limb buds form from the **somatic layer of the lateral plate mesoderm** covered by ectoderm, and this mesoderm makes the limb **bones, cartilage, tendons and connective tissue**. Limb **muscle** cells migrate in from the somites, so removing the somites leaves a well-formed but muscle-free limb. The **sclerotome** is tempting because it is a skeleton-forming part of the somite, but it builds the **axial** skeleton (vertebrae and ribs), not the limb bones.
questions.explanation_pt: Os brotos dos membros se formam a partir da **camada somática do mesoderma da placa lateral**, coberta por ectoderma, e esse mesoderma forma os **ossos, cartilagens, tendões e tecido conjuntivo** do membro. As células **musculares** do membro migram dos somitos, então retirar os somitos deixa um membro bem formado, mas sem músculo. O **esclerótomo** é tentador por ser a parte do somito que forma esqueleto, mas ele constrói o esqueleto **axial** (vértebras e costelas), não os ossos dos membros.

questions.stem: In an experiment on early chick embryos, researchers cut away the thick ridge of ectoderm that runs along the tip of a growing wing bud. The underlying mesoderm and the rest of the embryo are left untouched, and the embryo keeps developing normally. Which outcome in that wing is most likely?
choices: Ventral features on both the upper and lower surfaces
A short limb that lacks its distal parts
A limb of normal length without skeletal muscle
questions.explanation: The **apical ectodermal ridge** releases **FGF**, which keeps the mesoderm under it dividing so the limb grows from proximal to distal. Removing it stops outgrowth, giving a **truncated limb**; the earlier the removal, the more proximal the level of the missing parts. **Mirror-image digit duplication** is the classic result of grafting extra **zone of polarizing activity** (Sonic hedgehog) tissue to the anterior side of the bud, which affects the anterior-posterior axis rather than outgrowth.
questions.explanation_pt: A **crista ectodérmica apical** libera **FGF**, que mantém o mesoderma abaixo dela em divisão para que o membro cresça de proximal para distal. Retirá-la interrompe o crescimento e gera um **membro truncado**; quanto mais cedo a retirada, mais proximal o nível das partes que faltam. A **duplicação em espelho dos dedos** é o resultado clássico de enxertar tecido extra da **zona de atividade polarizante** (Sonic hedgehog) no lado anterior do broto, o que afeta o eixo anteroposterior e não o crescimento.

questions.stem: A 10-month-old girl is brought to the clinic for white patches of skin that have been present since birth. She has a white lock of hair at the front of the scalp and sharply outlined white patches on the center of the forehead, the middle of the chest and abdomen, and both knees. The patches have not changed in size since birth. Her father has the same pattern. Her eyes, hearing and development are normal. A skin biopsy from a white patch shows a normal epidermis with no melanocytes. The missing cells normally come from which embryonic tissue?
questions.explanation: This is **piebaldism**, usually caused by an inherited **KIT** mutation that stops **melanoblasts** from migrating to, or surviving in, parts of the skin. Melanoblasts come from the **neural crest** and travel to the epidermis and hair follicles, so the patches are present at birth and stay stable. The **surface ectoderm** is tempting because it forms the epidermis, but it makes the **keratinocytes**, which are normal here; only the pigment cells are missing.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **piebaldismo**, geralmente causado por uma mutação herdada no gene **KIT** que impede os **melanoblastos** de migrar para algumas áreas da pele ou de sobreviver nelas. Os melanoblastos vêm da **crista neural** e migram para a epiderme e os folículos pilosos, por isso as manchas existem desde o nascimento e ficam estáveis. O **ectoderma superficial** é tentador porque forma a epiderme, mas ele forma os **queratinócitos**, que aqui estão normais; só faltam as células pigmentares.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old basketball player lands on another player's foot, and his right ankle rolls inward while his toes are pointed down. He can walk four steps with pain. There is swelling and tenderness just in front of and below the lateral malleolus. The bone at the tip and back edge of both malleoli and at the base of the fifth metatarsal is not tender. With the lower tibia held still, pulling the heel forward moves the talus forward more on the right than on the left. Tilting the heel inward shows the same movement on both sides, and squeezing the calf causes no ankle pain. Which ligament is most likely torn?
questions.explanation: Inversion of a **plantar-flexed** foot strains the **anterior talofibular ligament** first, the weakest lateral ligament; it stops the talus from sliding forward, so its tear gives a positive **anterior drawer** test of the ankle. The **calcaneofibular ligament** tears next in more severe sprains and is tested by tilting the heel inward (**talar tilt**), which is normal here. A tear of the **anterior inferior tibiofibular ligament** (*high ankle sprain*) follows external rotation and causes pain when the calf is squeezed.
questions.explanation_pt: A inversão do pé em **flexão plantar** estira primeiro o **ligamento talofibular anterior**, o ligamento lateral mais fraco; ele impede que o tálus deslize para a frente, então sua ruptura torna positivo o teste da **gaveta anterior** do tornozelo. O **ligamento calcaneofibular** rompe em seguida nas entorses mais graves e é testado inclinando o calcanhar para dentro (**inclinação talar**, *talar tilt*), que aqui está normal. A ruptura do **ligamento tibiofibular anteroinferior** (*high ankle sprain*, entorse alta do tornozelo ou lesão da sindesmose) ocorre após rotação externa e causa dor ao apertar a panturrilha.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old rock climber slips and saves himself by grabbing a ledge with his right hand, so that his whole body weight pulls his arm straight up above his head. Two days later, his vital signs are: pulse 72/min, blood pressure 122/76 mm Hg. He cannot spread or bring together his right fingers, and the fingers rest bent at the middle and end joints with the knuckle joints extended. Grip is weak. Sensation is reduced along the inner side of the right forearm and hand. The right upper eyelid droops slightly, and the right pupil is smaller than the left. Shoulder abduction, elbow flexion and the biceps reflex are normal. Injury to which nerve roots best explains these findings?
questions.explanation: Strong upward pull on the arm stretches the **lower part of the brachial plexus** (**Klumpke palsy**). The **C8-T1** fibers supply the **intrinsic hand muscles**, so the fingers claw and cannot spread, and they carry sensation from the medial forearm and hand; the **T1 root** also carries the sympathetic fibers to the eye, so **Horner syndrome** (ptosis, miosis) appears. **C5-C6** injury (Erb palsy) follows forceful widening of the neck-shoulder angle and weakens shoulder abduction and elbow flexion, which are normal here.
questions.explanation_pt: Uma tração forte do braço para cima estira a **parte inferior do plexo braquial** (**paralisia de Klumpke**). As fibras de **C8-T1** inervam os **músculos intrínsecos da mão**, então os dedos ficam em garra e não se afastam, e conduzem a sensibilidade da face medial do antebraço e da mão; a **raiz T1** também leva as fibras simpáticas para o olho, então surge a **síndrome de Horner** (ptose, miose). A lesão de **C5-C6** (paralisia de Erb) ocorre após aumento forçado do ângulo entre pescoço e ombro e enfraquece a abdução do ombro e a flexão do cotovelo, que aqui estão normais.
